summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -4 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +4.7%; weakest: Lean hogs -17.5%. Key releases ahead: US Core CPI m/m (11-10 8:30 AM ET); US CPI m/m (11-10 8:30 AM ET); US Core PPI m/m (11-13 8:30 AM ET); US PPI m/m (11-13 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.88% (-36 bp in a month), 2-year 4.56% (-24 bp); 2s10s curve +32 bp (-12 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.04% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.66 (-0.5% in a month, +3.4% YTD). USD/BRL 5.508 (+9.8% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.672 (-0.4%); USD/MXN 18.53 (+1.9%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -3.3% in a month (+10.3% YTD); VIX 19.9. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 86.42 $/bbl (-5.0% in a month), Brent 92.20, ULSD 4.195 $/gal (-8.6%), natural gas 3.21 (-9.6%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -4.7% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.0%, Hang Seng +1.0%, yuan +0.4% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 6 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (18%); S&P GSCI -7.3% in a month; gold -1.6%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
